Prevention: Remove and burn all crop residues after harvest.
Interplant potatoes with repellent non-host crops such as onion and garlic.
Do not plant new potato crops next to infected fields.
Practice good field hygiene/ remove weeds.
Do not rotate with eggplant, okra, tomato, cotton, bean or cassava.

Monitoring: Look for tiny, reddish, spider- like mites underneath the leaves at least every two weeks and make a spraying decision.
Look for bruises on the young and large leaves, including the stems.
Look for the presence of chlorosis areas, that join to form mottled yellowish interveinal patches.
Look for the presence of spider webs on leaves and stems produced by the spider mites.
Start to control when there is an average of 8-12 mites per leaf.
Direct Control (Non-chemical): Remove and burn all infested plants.
Usually infestation starts with a few plants (a hotspot) and spreads with time.
Uprooting and burning hotspot plants can help.
Use a water spray to wash off mites if the infestation is not too heavy.
Use insecticidal soaps (neem- based) or neem-based products such as nimbecine (Azadiractin + neem oil).
Spray a mixture of 1 teaspoon of liquid soap in 4 litres of water or 50g (one quarter bar of 250g) soap in 20L of water.
Direct Control (Chemical): Use personal protective equipment when handling and applying pesticides, follow the label recommendations.
Do not eat, drink, smoke when mixing or applying pesticides.
C 44EC) at the rate of 12ml in 10L of water when pest appears.
ProclaimFit at rate of 1ml/L of water.
EC (Propargite) at 5ml/10L of water when the pest reaches the action threshold.
Spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon.
Restrictions: Observe a re-entry interval of 1 day and a pre- harvest interval of 7 days. (Spray in sufficient water.
Ensure full coverage of the plants).
